game: DAL @ HOU, Week 4 2026 (morning of kickoff; spread/total not saved)

script.base: No spread, total, or moneyline was saved, so the book’s expected leader and point total are unknown and no blowout flag can be set. From three games only, Dallas is the more explosive offense: Lamb 25 targets/309 yards/311 air, Pickens 25/150/267, Williams 43 carries/169 (3.93 YPC) plus 12 targets. Houston’s run game is stuck (Montgomery 37/103, 2.78 YPC; Marks 22/65, 2.95 YPC) and the pass game runs through Schultz (25 targets/205 yards) with inefficient deep air to Hutchinson (21 targets, 120 yards on 290 air). Houston blitzes only 23% and Dak’s EPA/dropback is 0.45 unblitzed vs 0.03 blitzed, so the base flow is competitive and Dallas pass-lean, with Houston mixing a low-efficiency run and Schultz targets rather than a declared Dallas runaway.
script.flip1: Dallas jumps ahead early and clocks it: Williams’s carries spike and his rush-under dies, while Lamb/Pickens yardage stalls the way a lead-and-run script stalls a QB (Lamb already has a 44-yard game as the template) and Houston abandons the run so Montgomery’s carries die and Stroud/Schultz/Hutchinson volume rises.
script.flip2: Either a slog — Houston’s run defense (3.59 YPC, only 6 runs of 10+) stuffs Williams and Clowney/Hall (both questionable) play and speed Dak into checkdowns — or a pass shootout if the missing safeties/LBs (Stewart, Overshown, Durant, Al-Shaair) turn both middle splits (HOU 10.11 YPA, DAL 9.0 YPA) into a Lamb-and-Schultz game. Weather cannot be used as a third flip; it was not saved.

injury_fallout: No offensive skill player is Out, so there is no next-man usage spike. HOU S M.J. Stewart Out (knee) vacates the deep safety and helps Dallas deep/middle shots, chiefly Lamb (311 air yards) and Pickens (267 air); the replacement is not named. DAL CB Cobie Durant Out (hamstring) thins the secondary Houston WRs see (Hutchinson 21 targets, Noel, Boutte, Collins). DAL LB DeMarvion Overshown Out (hamstring) is the coverage loss that helps Houston’s short/middle options — Schultz (25 targets), Marks/Montgomery as receivers, Noel. HOU LB Azeez Al-Shaair Out (groin) and Jake Hansen Questionable (calf) help Dallas RB/TE catches (Williams 12 targets, Ferguson 11). HOU DE Jadeveon Clowney Questionable (knee) and DE Logan Hall Questionable (knee): if both sit, Dallas pressure should fall, deep WR yards up and Dak scramble need down; if both play, the opposite. HOU G Ed Ingram Questionable (groin): if he sits, Houston rush efficiency (already 2.78/2.95 YPC) gets worse and quick throws to Schultz/RBs rise. Collins is the role uncertainty, not an injury tag: only 10 targets and 75 yards in the L3 pack, yet a 73.0 receiving line with no two-sided price. Sources: pack offense/defense weeks 1–3 and the pre-game nflverse injury report. Final inactives (~90 min pre-kick) are not in the pack.

matchup.shell: Man/zone and MOFO/MOFC rates are not charted (coverage charting absent). Location splits are the shell proxy. HOU: left 3.89 YPA on 27 attempts (locked), middle 10.11 on 27, right 9.48 on 42 — they bleed the middle and the right, not the boundary left. DAL: left 7.17 on 36, middle 9.0 on 17, right 6.84 on 31 — middle is the soft spot on a small sample.
matchup.pressure: HOU blitz 23%; Dak EPA/dropback 0.03 vs blitz and 0.45 vs no blitz, so Dallas wants Houston’s low blitz rate and should not be forced into checkdowns. DAL blitz 27%; Stroud EPA/dropback 0.42 vs blitz and -0.13 vs no blitz, so Dallas pressure helps Houston’s passing EPA rather than killing it. Clowney and Hall are only questionable, so the pass-rush picture is not locked.
matchup.bleeds: HOU run defense does not bleed: 3.59 YPC allowed, only 6 runs of 10+ in 3 games. HOU pass defense does: middle 10.11 YPA, right 9.48, and 13 passes of 20+ (13/107). DAL run defense bleeds: 5.23 YPC, 15 runs of 10+. DAL pass explosives are more contained (7/86) even though the middle is 9.0 YPA.
matchup.overlap: The clean overlap is Lamb, the Dallas primary (25 targets, 309 yards, 311 air), into the exact HOU weakness (middle/right, 13 explosives, Stewart out) with Houston blitzing too rarely to take the air yards away. Secondary overlap, not a selected leg: Schultz (25 targets, 205 yards) into DAL’s middle (9.0 YPA) with Overshown out. Williams rush is the inverse overlap: lead carry share into a run defense that does not bleed.

form: Avoiding season averages; L3 role only. Lamb 44/153/112 receiving, WR1 share stable, one quiet game. Pickens 28/40/82 on 267 air yards but only 150 yards — inefficient, and 69.5 sits above the 50-yard mean. Flournoy 22/23/22 on 18 targets/67 yards; 33.5 is above every game, but that is an averages tell, and the HOU safety absence argues against treating the under as a matchup read. Williams rush 41/30/98 (mean 56.3, median 41) on 43 carries; receiving 31/20/5; rush+rec 72/50/103. Dak rush 14/26/19, all over 10.5, averages-only. Ferguson 6/43/23 around 24.5. Montgomery rush 60/10/33 (mean 34.3 vs a 44.5 line) at 2.78 YPC; rec 19/14/15. Marks rush 42/8/15 (mean 21.7 vs 36); rush+rec 40/35/21, all under 49.5, but DAL’s 5.23 YPC allowed is the counter. Stroud rush 15/29/10 vs 10.5 (the 10 loses the over). Hutchinson 32/37/51, all over 26.5, but 290 air yards became only 120 yards and Collins still has a 73 line. Schultz 35/140/30 — median 35, mean spiked by one 140. Noel 53/31/17 trending down, all still over 11.5. Boutte 21/37/21 around 23.5. Moreau 15/34/7. Collins only a 75 listed.

pre_mortem: Monday morning the Lamb over lost because Dallas led early, Prescott’s dropbacks stalled, and the 44-yard game repeated — or Houston bracketed Lamb after 153 and 112 and Pickens took the deep shots into the backup safety, or Clowney and Hall both played and the ball came out to Williams and Ferguson. That counter is real but weaker than 25 targets, 311 air yards, a 10.11 middle YPA, and Stewart out, so the leg stays. The Williams under lost because he ripped another long run (the 98 already happened once, and Houston has allowed 6 runs of 10+) or because a Dallas lead gave him 18–22 clock-kill carries at a modest YPC and he cleared 58.5 anyway. That counter is close — the mean is only 2 yards under the line — which is why this is a lean, not a strong, and why it is tagged script-dependent. It is not stronger than the 3.59 YPC matchup, so it is not dropped.
slip_story: One story only: a competitive game that does not become a Dallas runaway. Lamb recyds over needs Dallas pass volume; Williams rushyds under needs his carries to stay near 14 against a 3.59 YPC defense. Those win together in the base script and in a Dallas-trailing script; both die if Dallas blows it open and clocks it (flip1). Do not add a Williams rush over, a Dallas team-total blowout, Schultz over (needs the 140 to repeat), Montgomery over (form and Ingram questionable fight the DAL 5.23 YPC bleed), or any TD. No third or fourth leg survived the pre-mortem. No bets placed.
